diagnosis.strongest: ALLR: one removed fallback did what two rounds of styling could not -- the board now says something no template site says, that 12 of its 16 organisations have made no claim about their own newest model, and it says it by drawing the hole.
diagnosis.weakest: The claim half of the same column: with the chip correctly gone, nothing on the page says in words that the four surviving cells are unverified vendor speech, and at 390 the whole column is off-frame.
diagnosis.critical_issue: None. Question 5 moves FAIL to PASS against the anchor on the same observable it failed on -- zero hatched cells became 12 of 96, in both themes, in the first viewport at 1440.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Put the blank's count in words in the lede: it labels the claim column's status, reaches 390 where the column does not, and gives the home door a number to carry -- one sentence closing all three new findings.

downstream.weakness: The identity now depends on a data condition holding: if the feeds fill those 12 cells, the signature disappears with no code change and no gate failure.
downstream.cause: The move is defined as the absence of data rather than as a stated property of the board, so its visibility is a function of the day's feed rather than of the design.
downstream.recommendation: Have the board state its own blank count as text next to the hatch, so the statement survives the day the data fills in; keep the S22 hatch floor as the alarm if it does.
